bel_linen_librarian.text: Hush now. Well, a wee bit hush. Welcome to the Linen Hall Library.
We were founded in 1788, which makes us the oldest library in Belfast. We are still going, and still very patient.
The name comes from the White Linen Hall, where cloth merchants once traded. The library lived there for nearly a century.

then.text: The Mill's open and the kettle's on. Go and look at it. You earned the first cup.
Go and see the Mill. South side, past the sandwich bar. The door's open.
You've been to the yard, the mill and the Wall. And you came back. That's more than most committees manage.
{player} tells Nuala about the heater boys, the half-timers and the men who built the Wall by hand.
That's the three testimonies. I'll write them up as they were told to you, and I'll put the names in. Heater boys, doffers and wallers all.
The old mill on the south side is open as of this morning. Mervyn cut the chain himself, with a bolt-cutter he says he 'found'. Go and see it.

else.text: Read the plaque beside the gap, then come back to me. Three trades, three stories.

then.text: Read the plaque beside the gap, then come back to me. Three trades, three stories.
The waller will have a gap for you to mend. Big stones low, joints covered.
Now the Mournes. There's a waller by the Wall who'll tell you how it went up.
The weaver at Lisburn Road Linens. Let her tell it her own way. It will take a while.
Lisburn Road Linens next. A bolt of linen on the table, and an old weaver who remembers the mills.
The plaque by the yard door, then. The 1907 strike. It is the bit they leave off the tea towels.
Sing with the yard singer, then read the 1907 plaque by the yard door. That's the yard done.
Mervyn Hanna next. He is about the streets of Belfast, and he'll be at the yard before long. Bring him champ if you can. Tea won't do.

else.text: Titanic Belfast has a board of the yard's records. Read it, then find Mervyn Hanna. He was forty-four years in the yard.
Mind the tea. It's been there since Tuesday and it has opinions.

I'm Nuala Orr. I keep the Local Studies shelves. Belfast made three things the whole world wanted: ships, linen, and the water that comes out of the tap. Every one was made by hand, and nobody wrote the hands down.

There's an old mill on the south side, shut for decades. The Council will knock it down unless somebody shows them what it's worth. I want to open it as a workshop for the three trades: the yard, the mill and the Wall.
Help Nuala gather the three testimonies?

then.text: Sure that's grand. The offer will keep, the mill won't.

else.text: Start with the yard. Read the board at Titanic Belfast, then find Mervyn Hanna. Forty-four years in the yard and he'll tell you if I've got it wrong.
Then the mill, and then the Wall. Three trades, three stories. Don't let anyone give you a tea towel instead.
